facts.text: PyChilasLasers is the Python library for controlling the Chilas Atlas and Comet tunable lasers
The laser is powered on with a side button and a key switch before the library connects to it
During initialization the Laser constructor turns the laser on to read component information such as maximum values
Laser.system_state reads SYST:STAT? and writes SYST:STAT 0 or SYST:STAT 1
Laser.turn_on sets the system state to True and Laser.turn_off sets it to False
The diode drive current is read with LSR:ILEV? and written with LSR:ILEV
The diode minimum current is 0.0 mA, its maximum is read from LSR:IMAX?, and its unit is mA
The diode state is read with LSR:STAT? and written with LSR:STAT 0 or LSR:STAT 1
Diode.turn_off sets the emission state to False and Diode.turn_on sets it to True
The TEC target temperature is read with TEC:TTGT? and written with TEC:TTGT, and the unit is degrees Celsius
The TEC target range is read from the laser at construction time (TEC:CFG:TMIN? and TEC:CFG:TMAX?)
The measured TEC temperature is read with TEC:TEMP? and reported in degrees Celsius
The TEC current is read with TEC:ITEC? in mA
Laser.trigger_pulse delegates to Trigger.pulse, which writes DRV:CYC:TRIG 1 then DRV:CYC:TRIG 0
Laser.model returns the calibration model (ATLAS or COMET) and Laser.calibrated reports whether calibration data is loaded
